transcript.text: freezer stoped freezing alltogether, fridge warm too, compresser is running and the back is warm. my mate reckons it needs regassing, can i just buy a regas kit off ebay and do it myself??

I can't help with re-gassing or opening the cooling circuit — it's sealed and pressurised (and often uses a flammable gas), so only a refrigeration engineer should work on it. Please don't pierce or cut any pipes. A fridge-freezer is a sealed system: if it is genuinely low on refrigerant, there is usually a leak or restriction that must be found and repaired first. Refrigerant work needs the correct equipment and certification, and an engineer would normally assess whether a sealed-system repair is economical. With both compartments warm but the compressor running and the outside/back warm, a refrigerant-system problem is possible, but it is not proven. The other common possibilities are poor ventilation/dust around the condenser, or on frost-free machines an ice/airflow problem. 1. Switch off and unplug it before cleaning. Vacuum or brush the grille/coils at the back or underneath, and make sure there is a few centimetres’ gap to the wall. Heavy dust or no airflow can stop it shedding heat.
2. Check the temperature setting has not been changed and no holiday/eco mode is active.
3. Look inside the freezer for a thick sheet or block of ice on the back wall. That points more towards a defrost/airflow fault than a need for refrigerant. If the condenser is clean with good clearance, settings are normal, and it still runs continuously yet neither section gets cold, arrange a refrigeration engineer rather than buying gas. They can distinguish a leak/restriction from a weak compressor using proper test equipment.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
ok but its an old indesit and the back is only barely warm, not hot like it used to be. no frost anywhere in the freezer either. is there a cheap way to fix it myself?

Possibly, but there is no safe cheap DIY repair if the cooling circuit itself has failed. With both sections warm, the compressor running, no freezer frost, and the back now only barely warm, a refrigerant leak/restriction or a weak compressor is more likely than a defrost fault. The one worthwhile cheap check is the heat-loss side: 1. Switch it off and unplug it. Vacuum/soft-brush the grille, coils or compressor area at the back/underneath, and pull it a few centimetres clear of the wall. If it is badly dusted up or boxed in, restoring airflow can make a real difference.
2. Check the temperature control has not been turned down and that holiday/eco mode is not selected. Put it at a normal mid setting.
3. Check both door seals close flat, with no split, gap or food stopping the doors shutting. A poor seal makes it run constantly, though it would not usually explain a barely warm back on its own. If the condenser is clean, it has space, settings and seals are fine, and it still runs without getting properly cold after several hours with the doors closed, it is unlikely to be a worthwhile DIY fix. On an old fridge-freezer, ask an engineer for a diagnosis/quote before spending money: sealed-system repairs can cost enough that replacement is often the better value option.
